themes_detail.label: Traffic surge in Crown Heights
themes_detail.summary: Traffic complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 433% increase (z-score: 6.24)—suggesting a sudden, acute disruption to street conditions that warrants immediate investigation into causes and impacts on commuters and residents.
evidence: 6 traffic complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over 8-week baseline (433% spike, z-score: 6.24)
Most recent spike in district with no obvious context provided in permit or development data
Acute emergence suggests infrastructure event, accident, or new construction impact
reporting_angles: Interview DOT or NYPD to identify what triggered this week's traffic surge and whether it's expected to continue
Canvass residents and businesses on affected streets to document commute delays and street access impacts

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary conditions surge last week
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints jumped 118% last week to 117 complaints versus a 53.6 per week baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 7.99), indicating a significant sanitation crisis that may reflect accumulating waste, rodent issues, or service gaps in the district.
evidence: 117 unsanitary condition complaints last week vs. 53.6 weekly average (118% spike, z-score: 7.99)
Unsanitary conditions rank #4 overall in 90-day complaint volume (738 total), indicating persistent baseline issue now worsening
No recent news coverage or community board data available to explain cause
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation to identify what neighborhoods were hit hardest and whether collection delays or service cuts occurred
Interview residents and local business owners about visible waste, rodent activity, or health concerns on their blocks

themes_detail.label: Illegal tree damage spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints surged to 6 last week versus a 0.6 per week baseline—an 860% spike (z-score: 6.27)—suggesting coordinated or widespread unauthorized pruning, cutting, or removal affecting the district's canopy.
evidence: 6 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (860% spike, z-score: 6.27)
499 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (304 alterations), some possibly involving tree removal during construction
FRESH Pt. 2 Atlantic Ave development in pipeline—may be driving contractor activity or illegal clearing
reporting_angles: Check DOB records to identify which active construction permits may include tree removal and whether violations were filed
Interview Parks Department about the nature of complaints and whether specific blocks or developments are involved

themes_detail.label: Electrical hazards emerging
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints jumped 1100% last week to 3 complaints versus a 0.2 per week baseline (z-score: 6.35), a sharp spike that may signal infrastructure failures, illegal wiring, or fire hazards affecting residential or commercial properties.
evidence: 3 electrical complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
304 alteration permits filed in last 90 days; electrical work often precedes fires or safety incidents if non-compliant
Community board has standing budget request for 'additional building inspectors'—suggests ongoing inspection capacity gaps
reporting_angles: Request DOB complaint details to identify whether complaints are residential, commercial, or infrastructure-related and which neighborhoods
Contact FDNY to cross-reference electrical complaints with recent fire calls or safety inspection failures

themes_detail.label: Construction and plumbing strain 2 weeks ago
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints spiked 227% two weeks ago to 38 complaints versus an 11.6 per week baseline (z-score: 4.54), alongside 642 plumbing complaints in the 90-day total—indicating sustained infrastructure stress and possible disruption from active building work.
evidence: 38 general construction/plumbing complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 11.6 weekly average (227% spike, z-score: 4.54)
Plumbing ranks #6 in overall 90-day volume with 642 complaints; heat/hot water is #1 with 3,529 complaints
102 new building permits and 13 demolitions filed in last 90 days; disruptions to water/sewer service likely during active work
reporting_angles: Interview DEP about whether recent construction permits are causing water main breaks or service interruptions
Cross-reference active construction permits with addresses of high plumbing complaint clusters
